questions.q: At the 'source (OLTP)' stage of the BI pipeline, where does T-SQL show up?
options: In every SELECT, JOIN, subquery, and stored procedure written against the transactional database, like AdventureWorks2012
T-SQL is never used at the source stage
Only in the reporting layer, never at the source
Only inside Power BI's own query engine
questions.explain: The source/OLTP stage is exactly what Chapters 1-9 of this course covered.

questions.q: How does T-SQL show up at the 'transform (ETL/ELT)' stage?
options: An INSERT...SELECT with dimension-key lookups can itself be the transform engine in an ELT pipeline, as shown in Lesson 112
T-SQL cannot be used for any transformation work
Only Python can perform transformations in a BI pipeline
Transformation always happens before any T-SQL is involved
questions.explain: Lesson 112 showed exactly this: T-SQL can be the transformation engine when the destination performs the transform itself.

questions.q: Why does Chapter 10's performance tuning apply at every stage of the pipeline?
options: A slow OLTP query, a slow ELT transform, and a slow warehouse aggregate are all diagnosed with the same execution-plan and STATISTICS IO tools
Performance tuning only matters for the final BI reporting stage
Chapter 10's tools only work on AdventureWorks2012, not AdventureWorksDW2014
Performance tuning is unrelated to any pipeline stage
questions.explain: The diagnostic tools from Chapter 10 are general-purpose and apply regardless of which stage the slow query lives in.

questions.q: In the lesson's closing example query, which course concepts are combined?
options: A JOIN, GROUP BY, a SARGable WHERE predicate, and a window function for a running total, run against a star-schema fact table
Only a single SELECT statement with no other concepts
Only concepts from Chapter 1
Only concepts related to constraints and normalization
questions.explain: That one query intentionally draws on Chapters 3, 4, 9, 10, and 12 all at once.

questions.q: What does the lesson suggest as a next step after finishing this course?
options: LTV Academy's standalone Power BI course, which picks up by connecting to AdventureWorksDW2014 and building dashboards on top of it
There is no suggested next step
Retaking Chapter 1 from scratch
Switching to a completely unrelated programming language
questions.explain: The Power BI course is a natural continuation, using the same warehouse this course built familiarity with.
